mark_breakdown.desc: Applying the addition rule $\text{P}(A \cup B) = \text{P}(A) + \text{P}(B) - \text{P}(A \cap B)$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The addition law of probability states $\text{P}(A \cup B) = \text{P}(A) + \text{P}(B) - \text{P}(A \cap B)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Sign errors when rearranging the equation.

subparts.stem: What can you say about $A$ and $B$?
subparts.final_answer: $A \text{ and } B \text{ are mutually exclusive events.}$

mark_breakdown.desc: Conclude that $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive because $\text{P}(A \cap B) = 0$

subparts.solution: Since $\text{P}(A \cap B) = 0$, $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Two events $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive (or disjoint) if and only if $\text{P}(A \cap B) = 0$.
step_by_step: Recall the definition of mutually exclusive events: they cannot occur at the same time, meaning $\text{P}(A \cap B) = 0$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing mutually exclusive with independent (independent means $\text{P}(A \cap B) = \text{P}(A)\text{P}(B)$).
